key_insight: Raising argon flow from 1600 to 1800 L/h during air plasma spraying of NiCrFeBSiC coatings produces thicker, denser coatings with better tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: This points to argon flow as a practical process-control lever for improving wear resistance and coating quality in thermal spray applications.
method: Air plasma sprayed self-fluxing NiCrFeBSiC metal-ceramic coatings at two argon flow rates: 1600 and 1800 L/h.
Characterized coating structure and mechanical properties using porosity/thickness analysis, microhardness, elastic modulus, and scratch testing.
Evaluated friction and wear behavior with ball-on-disk tribological tests.
evidence_signal: At 1800 L/h, coating thickness roughly doubled, porosity decreased by about twofold, and the friction coefficient dropped to approximately 0.107, with similar critical scratch loads but smoother failure progression.
watch_item: The study compares only two argon flow settings, so broader process optimization and long-term service performance still need validation.
paper_title: EFFECT OF ARGON FLOW RATE DURING AIR PLASMA SPRAYING ON THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF NICRFEBSIC COATINGS
